title: OCC–FDIC Supervisory Intervention Framework — 2026
question: What did the OCC and FDIC change on August 27, 2026 about when examiners can demand fixes or take enforcement action against a bank?
bluf: On August 27 the OCC and FDIC rewrote when examiners can issue a nonbinding observation, a mandatory “matter requiring attention,” or support enforcement for an unsafe practice. Enforcement now needs a stated link from the bank's conduct to material financial harm or risk to the deposit insurance fund, while matters requiring attention keep a lower, forward-looking bar. That should cut process-only findings but makes examiners' judgments about materiality more contestable. The Fed did not join, so there is no single standard across bank regulators.

For access_state private_by_design, use metadata only and do not infer contents.
Preserve the package evidence cutoff, evidence_cutoff_note and any material-specific as_of date. Verify time-sensitive claims with fresh primary sources.
Keep fact, project inference, strongest rival, unresolved object and falsifier separate.
